canonical_statement: The study proposes ReTree to keep per-step search-agent reasoning context bounded while preserving source-linked evidence and enabling structural repair of downstream reasoning after evidence contradictions.

The problem formulation requires a useful search memory to satisfy bounded per-step context, traceability of answer claims to retrieved passages, and dependency-consistent revision of states derived from revised evidence.
ReTree represents memory as an external rooted evidence tree whose active node stores a compact task-state summary, locally introduced evidence, revision history, and a parent pointer.

The policy context is constructed from the active-node summary plus the top-5 lexically relevant evidence items; summaries are capped at 140 words, so per-step reasoning context is bounded with trajectory length while external storage may continue to grow.
Each search action returns up to five passages and the extractor emits at most six question-relevant atomic facts.
Each extracted fact is bound to its source by passage index rather than by asking the language model to reproduce a URL.
The query policy may stop only after at least one real retrieval and after evidence supports the final requested answer slot.

A backtrack is proposed only when new evidence supplies an incompatible value for the same entity and attribute under the same scope and time; refinements, different senses, and compatible candidates expand the tree instead.

A proposed backtrack is subjected to a second history-aware revision check using the branch summary, targeted evidence, new facts, and the target evidence change history, and repair is applied only for same-scope contradictions with better support.

When a conflict is confirmed, ReTree locates the node that introduced the refuted evidence, replaces that evidence and source, records the revision, regenerates the node summary from corrected evidence, prunes all descendants, and resumes search from the repaired node.

Final attribution decomposes reasoning into atomic claims linked to evidence identifiers, resolves each identifier to current evidence text and URL, and uses an NLI judge to test whether the cited raw passage entails the claim.
The current implementation selects top-k evidence by lexical overlap in O(|A(n)|) time and locates evidence introducers by tree traversal in O(|T|) time.
The benchmark evaluation includes 2,149 questions: all 125 Bamboogle questions, all 824 FRAMES questions, and fixed 600-question subsets of 2WikiMultiHopQA and HotpotQA.

canonical_statement: Answer quality is evaluated with GPT-5 judge accuracy against gold answers under type constraints and normalized exact match; provenance is evaluated with NLI-based citation precision, citation recall, and uncited rate on 600 FRAMES questions; context/compute metrics include maximum per-step policy context, model calls, and token usage.

outcome.measurement_method: GPT-5 answer judge, normalized EM, NLI-based passage entailment, rendered context characters, model-call and token counts

canonical_statement: All agent variants use Qwen3-8B, the same Google Search API backend and question order, a maximum of eight searches per question with up to five passages each, at least one retrieval before answering, seed 0, and fixed hyperparameters across benchmarks.

Local inference uses Qwen3-8B in FP16 through an OpenAI-compatible SGLang endpoint on two NVIDIA A40 48GB GPUs with Python 3.10.20, PyTorch 2.2.1, and CUDA 12.1; live web search and GPT-5 evaluation use hosted APIs.
Full-Trajectory ReAct retains the complete uncompressed observation trajectory and serves as the primary transcript-based baseline.

FlatUpdate shares ReTree’s 140-word summary, top-5 evidence budget, and conflict detector but stores evidence in a flat list and replaces a refuted fact without rebuilding dependent summaries or pruning downstream reasoning.

exposures.details: Flat evidence list with in-place fact replacement and no dependency-directed pruning

canonical_statement: Hard subtree pruning treats every descendant of a revised node as dependent, so it can invalidate useful downstream facts that are actually independent of the corrected premise.

Correction quality depends on the conflict judge: false negatives preserve contaminated state, whereas false positives can over-prune useful evidence; same-scope checks and revision history reduce but do not eliminate these errors.
Bounding per-step context does not bound total external memory: the evidence store grows with retrieval, and linear evidence selection and tree traversal can become slower over very long horizons.
Wall-clock latency was not reported because live-search network variance made it unstable as an evaluation metric.

The authors conclude that search-agent working memory should preserve a revisable dependency structure over evidence and intermediate conclusions rather than functioning only as a compressed transcript.
